reason: Workspace and user instruction files are kept as a contributor that enters sourced user-role messages; reads go only through the filesystem seam, loaded files are watched, links out of the project root are refused and each chain keeps a guaranteed budget.
The path-candidate service and the @file mention grammar are kept as one component over the workspace's filesystem seam; a mention stays text and content enters only through a logged read.

The host-local provider is folded into the fileref component: the filesystem seam is already the swappable part, so a second seam with one provider would add nothing. The bounded index, ranking and prompt section are kept.

The package exists only for developing upstream itself: its prompt text names the upstream checkout, its pnpm watcher and its client reload, and most of its code keeps earlier-format upstream sessions byte-stable. The general rule it applied (no per-process value in the system prompt) is kept as a rule for every contributor.

Session mentions and bounded, untrusted snapshots are kept as a resolver service and a required contributor; discovery and capture now take the caller's principal, and a truncated capture is saved through the spill store.
The clock reading is kept as a contributor with a fixed-size fold; the sampled instant is recorded in the message so a replay calls no clock, and the component is mounted per preset.

Terminal location is an opt-in user feature for a command-line session inside tmux, not a development aid, so it is kept as an off-by-default contributor at P2 that runs one read-only command through the shell seam.

The contract stays a separate package: the Engine interface, the compaction event types, the SummaryFailed event and the balanced-edge helpers. The log bracket becomes a record because the driver goroutine and the session lease already exclude a second compaction.

The threshold policy and model-written summary are kept as the basic provider; the result commits as one group, the summariser call is logged before it is sent and settled by one event per attempt, and failure is bounded per trigger.

The durable image/offload event and its pure rewrite are kept, bound statically to the payload version as area A01 requires; where a route declares an image budget the offload is planned before the request is sent.

Head, marker and tail pruning of oversized tool results is kept as a model-free reducer that appends a cited replacement; cuts now fall on line boundaries and the marker says how much was removed and where the full text is.
The human /compact command is kept as a host-side command that calls Engine.Now as a maintenance task; it now waits for idle, takes a focus text and a keep count, and is reachable from every carrier.

The provider registry is kept with one registration path, concurrent provider queries under a deadline, a kept last-good catalogue per provider, per-skill diagnostics and an inspectable list of shadowed definitions.

The local provider keeps the same roots, front matter and one-level layout; it reads through the filesystem seam, uses the shared watch service instead of private chokidar and polling code, and contains a failure to the one skill that caused it.

The router and three authoring skills are kept as data embedded in the binary and served by a provider; their text names the Go office tools of area A16 and points at the user's Python or one configured interpreter.

The catalogue, the skill tool and explicit user invocation are kept; the catalogue becomes a fold with deltas, the tool enforces invocation policy and a size cap in the pipeline, and plain-text invocation is limited to the first token of a message.

The package reports paths into a Python, Node.js and pnpm payload that upstream's desktop application and SDK wheel carry. The Go product is one pure-Go binary with nothing bundled or downloaded, so the tool would describe an artifact nobody builds; the Office skills point at the user's Python instead.

The Go command waits for the agent to become idle by default and then runs the compaction as a maintenance task; a caller may ask for an immediate compact/busy error instead. The wait is cancellable and queued prompts keep their order.

The command registry is host-side with one parser, so arguments no longer vary by adapter: /compact takes an optional focus text, which is logged in compaction/request, and keep=N to keep the last N turns verbatim. Arbitrary ranges stay the programmatic Engine.Region call.

Commands are a host service, not a client adapter, so the HTML UI, the SDK protocol, ACP and the command line reach the same /compact, and Engine.Now is a plain service call. It depends on areas A17, A20 and A24 exposing command invocation.
The trigger still rests on an estimate: area A04's meter is a deterministic fold with a per-session calibration factor, not a tokenizer.
justification: An exact count needs a provider tokenizer or a network call per measurement, which area A04 declined for its own token-meter limit. The effect is bounded here: the threshold keeps headroom below the window, and provider-confirmed overflow recovery is the backstop (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4).

reason: The summariser has an ordered route list (configured, answering route, latest header, the session's selected route). On a permanent failure of a candidate the engine moves to the next one only if it is the route the user selected for this session, and records the reason in compaction/request, so revoked credentials on the old model no longer block compaction.

A span whose estimate exceeds the summarising route's window is cut at balanced edges and summarised left to right, each call receiving the previous partial summary; nothing commits until the last call succeeds.

Classification stays with area A04 as a closed repairable failure code checked by a driver conformance table. This area adds a second signal so that changed provider wording does not disable recovery: a rejected request while the calibrated estimate is at least 95% of the window is treated once per step as a suspected overflow, logged with that trigger and bounded by maxOverflowRetries.
One of the two cases remains. A single oversized unit is now summarised from a pruned view. A system prompt plus tool list that alone approaches the window still cannot be shrunk by compaction.
justification: Compaction acts on derived history; the envelope is fixed by composition. The engine reports compact/envelope-too-large with the prompt and tool sizes so the operator can act, and deferred tool disclosure in area A03 is the mechanism that shrinks a tool list (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4).

reason: Engine.Region runs inside the caller's open turn or, on an idle agent, as a maintenance task; the owner recorded on compaction/start is the turn number or none, so a fully closed session can be compacted by range.

The surface is still left as it was on failure, which is the intended fail-safe, but failure is no longer only a warning: each failed call is a compaction/attempt event and a UI notice, the summariser uses the lowest reasoning effort so hidden reasoning cannot consume the output cap, and after maxConsecutiveFailures on one route the engine stops paying for a failing call at every step.

One price basis is chosen when the reduction is planned (the destination route for a model switch, the committed route otherwise) and is used both to select the span and to check that the summary is smaller, so a useful summary is not rejected by a second price.
An offloaded image stays offloaded when a budget grows or history shrinks.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6: restoring images automatically would make the model-visible image set depend on unlogged request preparation, which the upstream decision note rejects and outcome DH-O-4 forbids. The placeholder names a read-only path, and reading it creates a new, logged occurrence.

reason: Where the route's catalogue entry declares an image budget, the offload is planned at the proposed step before the request is sent, so no attempt fails; the provider's rejection remains the signal only for a route with an undeclared budget. It depends on area A04 publishing the budget.
A route with a small image budget, used briefly, still offloads images for the rest of the session.
justification: It follows from the stability rule of DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6: an omission, once logged, holds for every later request. The cost is bounded because the image bytes are kept and the placeholder path lets the model read one again as a new occurrence.

reason: Prune budgets are still character counts, not token counts.
justification: Kept on purpose: a character budget makes pruning a pure, idempotent function, so a pruned result is never pruned again, which a token estimate that moves with calibration would not guarantee. The meter decides whether pressure was relieved, and the transaction measures again after pruning (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6).

reason: Pruning keeps the head and the tail without judging which middle lines matter.
justification: Kept on purpose: a model-free reducer cannot rank lines, and ranking would need a model call. The limit is narrowed: cuts fall on line boundaries, the marker states how many characters were removed and where the full text is when area A07 spilled it, and the original result stays in the log (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6).

reason: A cut can still split a grapheme cluster in rare cases.
justification: Narrowed, not removed: a cut snaps to a line boundary where one lies inside the budget and is otherwise never placed before a combining mark, a variation selector or a zero-width joiner. Full Unicode text segmentation would need a new module for a cosmetic gain, and the original text is in the log (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-6).

reason: There is still no model-facing compaction tool.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4: a model that could compact at will could discard history the user relies on, and automatic pressure already covers the need. People compact through the command, and the model gets read-only recall of compacted spans at P2 (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-10).

reason: Tool results are bounded before they enter history and prunable afterwards, and a single non-tool unit that is still too large for the summariser is summarised from a pruned view of its text and replaced by that summary, with the original in the log.
A system prompt plus tool list that alone approaches the window is still not shrunk by compaction.
justification: Compaction acts on derived history; the envelope is fixed by composition and cannot be summarised without changing what the agent is. The engine reports compact/envelope-too-large with both sizes, and deferred tool disclosure in area A03 is the mechanism that shrinks a tool list (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-4).

reason: A cd inside a shell command still triggers no nested instruction discovery.
justification: Parsing shell text is not a reliable filesystem seam, as upstream says. The limit is narrowed: besides file-tool touches, the working-directory argument of a shell or terminal call and a change of the session working directory count as touches (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2; depends on areas A09 and A06).

reason: Loaded instruction files are watched through the shared watch service, and a notice marks the file for reconciliation at the next proposed step. Where watching is unavailable (polling mode, a remote workspace) loaded files are checked by metadata at each proposed step.
Lower-case names, rule directories and @path imports are still not interpreted, and user-global roots have no local overlay.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2: an import would let a repository file pull arbitrary paths into the prompt, and a rule directory multiplies the files that can steer the model. Other file names are available through the candidates config field.

reason: De-duplication is by content digest across the whole rendered chain, and the state is a registered fold holding one digest per path; a file is hashed again only when its size, time or identity changed, so the cached-metadata special cases are gone. A copy that has drifted is different content and renders, which is correct.

Failure is contained per file: an unreadable candidate keeps its own last-good digest and gets a diagnostic, while the other files of its group reconcile normally, so one unreadable root no longer postpones a notice for another.

A file dropped by the budget stays tracked as omitted with its digest and is evaluated again at every reconciliation; when room appears it is added as an additional-instructions message without rebuilding the baseline.

A project-chain candidate is resolved through the filesystem seam's rooted handle; if the target lies outside the project root it is refused, never read, and reported. Only the user's own global files may link elsewhere.
Instruction text is bounded and truncated, never summarised by a model.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-2: summarising would add a model call to every session start and make the guidance the model follows differ from the file the user wrote. The budget notice names what was omitted or truncated.

reason: Each chain is guaranteed maxBytes and the bytes one chain leaves unused are lent to the other, so a large user-global file is no longer truncated while the project chain is nearly empty; neither chain can push the other below its floor.

Candidates are listed through the filesystem seam of the session's workspace, the same seam the read tool uses, so local, sandboxed and remote workspaces each see their own namespace; the separate host-local provider is merged away.
The index is still bounded by maxEntries and still omits excluded or unreadable directories.
justification: Bounded memory is required by outcome DH-O-14. The limit is narrowed: ignore files shrink what is indexed, a query containing a slash lists the live directory whatever the bound, and the result carries a truncated flag that the UI shows (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9).

reason: The harness's own file mutations update the index from the fs.Observed notice of area A08, so a query right after a write sees it; changes made outside the harness are picked up by the background rebuild.
Discovery applies the workspace's ignore files through area A08's rule evaluator (respectIgnoreFiles, default true) in addition to the configured directory names.
The service no longer has a namespace of its own: the one implementation reads through the workspace's filesystem seam, so a candidate is by construction a path the read tool can open.
A mentioned file is still text; its content enters only when the model reads it.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9: content then arrives as a logged tool result under the read tool's bounds, which keeps outcome DH-O-4 simple, and a user who wants content attached uses attachments (area A07).

reason: A release that changes system-prompt text still rewrites the first system message on routes that cannot take an in-history prompt update.
justification: The package is dropped (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3), but this consequence is general and is governed by area A02's request-series rule: the prompt must be current, and the rewrite is a logged new series. This area keeps its own share out of the prompt: no contributor may put a per-process value there (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-1).

reason: No Go session has a per-process value in its system prompt, and the Go store reads no upstream session, so there is no earlier format whose values could persist for a session's lifetime.
The two sections are not built, so no binary can differ from another in having them; several hosts on one home assemble the same prompt sections.
The two sections and their runtime-context lines are not built, so no persona can keep guidance that points at values its requests never carry.
The sections are not built, so a resumed session has nothing of this kind added to its prompt.
No projection that recognises earlier prompt wording is built, because no Go session holds an earlier wording and upstream sessions are not read by the store.
Candidates accepts a mode: title, the default, or text, which uses the session search of area A06 over message bodies. Body search is scheduled at P2 inside the same deliverable.

In the Go store a title is a list column committed with its events (area A06), so every stored session has a label without folding a log, and no session lacks one for having been written before a cache existed.
Candidates and Prepare take the admitted caller's principal and apply the access filter, so a non-owner sees and captures only sessions it may read; the service is still not a model-facing tool.
Only the text of user and assistant messages crosses sessions.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9: images and tool results would need attachment references across sessions and a much larger budget, and tool output from another session is the least trustworthy content to import.

reason: A reference is a snapshot, not a live link to the other session.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-9: the snapshot in the target's log is what keeps the target's replay independent of the source session, as outcome DH-O-4 requires. The user mentions the session again to refresh it.

reason: A truncated capture is saved as plain text, each message under a header carrying a per-capture boundary token and with its own line breaks kept, so a literal phrase is searchable except across an original line break; reference-aware retention in area A07 keeps the file while a session event cites it.

Clock state is a registered fold of fixed size: the last reading, the last model-visible message time and the current turn's zones up to maxZonesPerTurn, after which the turn counts as mixed. A proposed step always concerns the driver's current turn, so the full-prefix scan fallback does not exist.
The reading guides interpretation; it does not fill another tool's zone argument.
justification: Kept on purpose: a tool that needs a zone must receive it explicitly so that the logged arguments say what was scheduled; filling it silently would hide a guess from the user and from the log.

reason: A turn holding prompts from different zones still tells the model to ask.
justification: Kept on purpose: guessing which zone owns an unqualified time is the error this context exists to prevent, so asking is the specified behaviour and a test pins it.

reason: A zone the user set in settings, or one an SDK client sends with the message, is authority when no browser zone is present; only the process zone remains a display fallback under the ask policy.
Readings still show whole seconds.
justification: Kept on purpose: sub-second digits cost tokens in every reading and no tool consumes them; event times in the log keep full precision.

reason: Clock readings still accumulate in history between compactions.
justification: History is append-only so that the provider's prefix cache stays valid; removing old readings would rewrite the prefix. The cost is bounded by the default ten-minute interval and by mounting the contributor only in presets that use it, and compaction removes old readings with their span (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-1).

reason: Location is still read on the first step of a turn only.
justification: Kept on purpose: a reading costs a process start and a pane rarely moves inside a turn; the next turn reports the change.

reason: Only the agent's own pane location is reported; sibling panes are never read.
justification: Kept on purpose: the text of sibling panes may hold secrets, and outcome DH-O-7 says secrets are not printed or logged. It is a guarantee, pinned by a test, not a gap.

reason: The layout tree is reported, not pixel sizes.
justification: Kept on purpose: sizes change on every resize and would defeat the rule that an unchanged location adds no message.

reason: The command asks tmux for fields joined by the ASCII unit separator, and the contributor rejects that character inside a field, so a window name cannot mis-split a reading.
Detection still relies on the POSIX controlling terminal; on Windows the contributor does nothing.
justification: tmux does not run natively on Windows, and matching the controlling terminal is what excludes a terminal that merely inherited tmux's environment. The contributor is off by default and adds nothing where the check cannot run.

reason: Discovery stays one level deep.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-CONTEXT-7: it bounds the scan and matches the layout other agent tools use for the shared skills directory; a nested tree would make skill names ambiguous.

reason: The project root comes from the shared resolver with configurable markers, the same one instruction files use, so a workspace without .git can name its own marker.
An invalid entry becomes a per-skill diagnostic in the registry; the catalogue the model sees names skipped skills, and the settings view shows the reason, so absent and invalid are distinguishable.
An unreadable skill is one diagnostic and its siblings stay listed. Only a failure to list the root itself marks the provider failed, and then its last-good catalogue is kept.
The provider holds no polling code: the shared watch service follows a path whose parent directories do not exist yet and attaches when they appear.

The digest of a loaded body is recorded on the tool result and folded; when the watched file later changes, the next step adds a one-line notice naming the skill. Old results are still not rewritten, which is correct for an append-only log.
The provider still installs no authoring libraries.
justification: Kept on purpose: the harness downloads and bundles nothing (DH-ADR-20, DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3). The skill text tells the model to check that the libraries import and to name what is missing instead of installing globally.

reason: LibreOffice output can still differ from native Office applications.
justification: Inherent to the engine the owner chose (DH-ADR-20); area A16 reports the engine version with each result, and the skill text states the difference so the model can tell the user.

reason: Legacy, encrypted and macro-enabled files still need another workflow.
justification: It is the scope of the skill content: legacy files are converted first through area A16's convert tool, and encrypted or macro-enabled files are outside what the authoring libraries handle. The skills say so instead of failing silently.

reason: The four skills are embedded in the binary and checked at start-up, so they cannot be missing after install; any skill problem from an override directory is a registry diagnostic shown in the settings view, not only a log line.
The embedded set is complete by construction, and an override directory that lacks one of the four fails the component's load with a diagnostic, so the router never names an absent subskill.
An override directory is served by the same watched filesystem provider code, which keeps no negative cache; restoring a file lists the skill at the next lookup without a restart.
A provider declares MaxAge: zero for one that invalidates itself, a duration for a source that cannot notify. The registry lists such a provider again once the age is exceeded.
Providers are asked concurrently, each under its own deadline, and merged in rank order; a slow provider delays only itself, and its context is cancelled at the deadline.

The registry keeps each provider's last-good catalogue and a status (ok, stale or failed, with the error). A failed provider's entries stay listed as stale, so a lower-ranked skill does not take over a name because its owner flickered.
Snapshot returns the shadowed definitions with the reason each one lost, and the settings view and the command line can list them.
A catalogue entry renders the description and, when present, whenToUse inside the length cap, and the loaded block states the skill's source class.
A body over maxBodyBytes is refused with skill/too-large, naming its size and path so the model can read it in parts; it is never truncated, because half an instruction file is worse than none.
The tool result lists up to maxResourceEntries files of the bundle directory, so the model knows what exists; contents are still read on demand with the file tools, as logged tool results.
Loading a skill is still one text result, with no partial or streaming form.
justification: Bounded instead of streamed: a body has a size cap and a provider has a deadline, and a larger body is read in pages with the file tools from the reported path. A streaming handle would add a second result form for a case the cap removes (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-8).

reason: The catalogue state is a fold, and a change is published as a delta of added, changed and removed names when that is smaller than the list; a removal still retires a name explicitly.
The loaded body's digest is recorded with the tool result; a later change of that body is announced once by a one-line notice at the next step, so the model knows the instructions it holds are stale.

The limit describes the Linux payloads that upstream's build script downloads and locks. The Go project builds no payload and the tool is not built (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3), so the limit exists only because of the upstream build process.

The limit describes executable permissions of a payload carried by upstream's Python wheel or desktop installer. No payload is built or carried in the Go design (DH-ADR-CONTEXT-3), so it exists only because of the upstream build and packaging process.

A total source budget (maxTotalSourceBytes) is checked against file sizes before any read in one baseline or reconciliation batch, most specific file first, which is the aggregate bound the marker asks for.

The project root is found once per working directory, recorded in the baseline message's source and held in the fold; it is recomputed only when the session's working directory changes, so editing a marker does not reinterpret existing scope keys.
The watch code is not ported: the provider uses the harness watch service specified in libs/chokidar.md and keeps only skill filtering and invalidation, which is the extraction the marker asks for.

The Go harness exposes the same tool, skill with one name argument, declared once in the tool registry. Changes: the result states the source class and lists bundle files, the invocation policy and a size cap are enforced in the pipeline, and the body digest is recorded.

No such tool is exposed: it locates a bundled Python, Node.js and pnpm payload, and the Go product bundles and downloads nothing. The Office skills state the user's Python or one configured interpreter path instead.

Replaced by the typed around key compact.SummaryFailed with the closed results GiveUp and Repaired; the image-offload component is its first listener and must record a durable change before asking for another request.
Replaced by the typed notify key skill.Changed carrying the scope and a revision, sent after a provider invalidation or registration commits; listener failures are contained.

Replaced by the Go struct instructions.Config: maxBytes per chain as a floor, maxSourceBytes, the new maxTotalSourceBytes, projectRootMarkers, candidates, localCandidates and agentsHome, decoded strictly.

Replaced by the Go struct basic.Config with upstream's fields and defaults, plus automatic headroom for small windows, the summariser's reasoning effort, maxConsecutiveFailures and per-route modelPolicies.
Replaced by the Go struct prune.Config with thresholdChars, headChars and tailChars at upstream's defaults and the rule that head, marker and tail fit the threshold.
Replaced by the Go struct fileref.Config: maxResults, maxEntries, excludedDirectories and the new respectIgnoreFiles.
Replaced by the Go struct sessionref.Config: maxReferences, candidateLimit, maxReferenceBytes and referenceContextFraction, with upstream's defaults and bounds.
Replaced by the Go struct skill.Config: cacheEntries, which keeps upstream's default of 128, and the new providerTimeout.

Replaced by the Go struct fsprovider.Config: root switches, customDirs, agentsHome, projectRootMarkers, watch and maxProjects. The chokidar tuning fields are gone because the shared watch service owns them.
Replaced by the Go struct office.Config: assetRoot, which defaults to the embedded set, and python, which is user or an absolute interpreter path.
Replaced by the Go struct clock.Config: timeZone, refreshInterval with upstream's ten-minute default, and the new maxZonesPerTurn that bounds fold state.
Replaced by the Go struct tmux.Config with the one field refreshInterval, default zero.
Replaced by the Go struct skilltool.Config: descriptionMaxLength with upstream's default of 500, and the new maxBodyBytes and maxResourceEntries.
The tool and its source and root fields are not built. The one choice the schema expressed, which Python the Office skills name, is carried by the python field of office.Config.
Replaced by the service key compact.Key with the interface Engine: Consider for automatic triggers, Now for an idle session and Region for an explicit span.
Replaced by the service key fileref.Key with one method, List, which returns ranked candidates and a truncated flag for one agent's workspace.
Replaced by the service key sessionref.Key with the interface Resolver: Candidates and Prepare, both taking the caller's principal.
Replaced by the service key skill.Key with the interface Registry: RegisterProvider, Snapshot and Load. The separate direct-registration method is replaced by the skill.Static provider helper.
Replaced by the service key prune.Key with the interface Pruner: Measure, PruneContent and PruneSession.

Kept as decided: the window is a fact of the exact route, read from area A04's catalogue; measurement stays model-agnostic; thresholds, retention and the summariser target are per-route policy of the compaction provider. One change: headroom defaults to the smaller of 65,536 tokens and a fifth of the window, so a small-window route does not silently lose automatic compaction.

Kept: a log-only image/offload event names exact image occurrences and a pure function applies it to every later request, so the visible image set is rebuilt from the log. Two changes: the function is bound statically to the event type and payload version (area A01), and where a route declares its image budget the offload is planned before the request is sent.

Kept as a composition rule: a contributor component is mounted in the presets whose tools use its message, and a contributor mounted in a preset serves only that preset's agents. The clock ships in presets that carry the schedule tools and not in the minimal one.

The skill structure is kept: a short router plus three authoring skills that the model loads by name, so ordinary edits do not pay for rendering guidance. The note's shell-execution and mounting parts were already superseded upstream by the Office tools and the cross-deployment note; in Go the skills name area A16's tools.

Kept: two ordered user-global files, the harness home's and the shared agents root's, de-duplicated by content so the common linked layout renders once. Two changes: de-duplication covers the whole chain, and an unreadable file keeps its own last-good state instead of sharing its group's fate.

Kept and extended: each chain is guaranteed its own byte budget so a large project chain cannot evict the user's rules, and the bytes one chain does not use are lent to the other, which removes the waste the note accepted. The note's objection to a shared budget (one chain starving the other) does not apply because the floor is guaranteed.

The outcome is kept by other means. Office skills are available in every composition because they are embedded in the binary instead of read from a package directory. The bundled Python environment and its pythonEnvironment switch are not built, since nothing is bundled; the skills name the user's Python or one configured interpreter. Locating the engine and reporting it unavailable belong to area A16 under DH-ADR-20.

The rule is kept and generalised: no per-process value may enter the system prompt, and changing facts are delivered as context, so a new port or checkout cannot change a session's prompt. The package that applied it to two development-only values, and its projection for earlier-format sessions, are not built.

Adopted in part as later scope. From the first build a checkpoint carries a code-written footer and compaction/summary lists the replaced events; at P2 two read-only tools read or search a compacted span of the caller's own session. The split into frozen index checkpoints and one state checkpoint is a second provider on the same seam, left undesigned because its cache benefit is unmeasured.

Adopted: instruction files are found and read only through the filesystem seam, which is a required injection, so local, sandboxed and remote workspaces behave alike and there is one set of error and cancellation paths. Unlike upstream, a missing filesystem provider is a load error, not a silent no-op.

Upstream rejected the removal to keep an extension path for plugins. Go keeps the path and takes the simplification: the registry has one way in, RegisterProvider; a compiled-in component uses the skill.Static helper, and a plugin process provides skills through a granted plugin-protocol call (area A22). The second ranking, validation and cache path is not built.

The rejection stands: the contract stays apart from its provider. In Go a small interface with one implementation costs little, and three reducers (the summariser, the pruner and image offload) plus a possible recall provider already sit behind the contract.

title: Context is a logged, sourced message produced by one ordered pipeline
Instruction files: one read path, two chains with a floor, contained links, watched
Two packages are not built: the development context and the bundled-runtime locator
Compaction is a seam whose result commits as one group; the bracket is a record, not a lock
The summarising call is a logged, attributed model request with bounded failure
Model-free reductions run first, and each is a logged replacement or a versioned rewrite
A skill is data with the trust of tool output, served through one provider path
The catalogue is a fold with deltas; the tool enforces invocation policy; explicit invocation is structured
A reference is a pointer or a snapshot, never a live link
Compacted history stays reachable; recall tools are later scope
The clock and the terminal location say little, on purpose
Context reaches the model through one logged, ordered pipeline
The agent follows the workspace's and the user's instruction files, and notices when they change
The model knows the time
A user can point at a file or at another session
A long session keeps working: history is summarised under pressure, on a model switch and after an overflow
Oversized tool output and old images are reduced without a model call
A person can compact a session on demand
Skills from the project, the user and the binary are found, merged and kept current
The model discovers skills in a catalogue and loads one with a tool; the user can invoke one directly
The model can read back what compaction replaced
The model can be told where its terminal is
A session can be mentioned by words of its messages
Replaying a recorded log rebuilds every request without reading a file, clock, shell or session
Context messages enter in table order, an unchanged observation adds nothing, and a shadowed baseline returns in the same step
An optional contributor's failure is skipped and recorded, a required one rejects the step, and a downstream reject enters nothing
Golden instruction rendering: chain order, overlays, de-duplication, the three message forms and frame escape
Instruction budgets: a floor per chain, lent bytes, the total source budget and the return of an omitted file
Instruction reconciliation on watch, touch, directory change and resume; per-file failure containment; a held project root; a link leaving the root is refused
Clock readings under virtual time: interval, elapsed time, zone policy, and fixed-size fold state
tmux output parsing with hostile names; a failed command or an unchanged location adds nothing
File mentions: grammar fuzzing, ranking, ignore files, incremental index update and the truncated flag
